meaning: A funny picture, video, or phrase that people copy, change, and pass along to each other online.
clues: It is a joke or idea that people keep copying and changing.
It spreads from person to person, usually on phones and computers.
A scientist named Richard Dawkins invented the word in a book from 1976.
It is often a photo with a funny caption written across it.
It has four letters and starts with M.
assumes: A GIF is a short looping animation
A selfie is a photo of yourself

decoys.meaning: A small picture file that can play a short animation again and again, with no sound.
A photo that you take of yourself, usually with a phone held out at arm's length.
A teasing headline or picture made to make you click, often for a story that disappoints.

exchange.speaker: floyd
exchange.text: Back in my day, a funny drawing got photocopied and pinned to the office board. It took all week to spread.

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: Now it takes minutes. Tip: if one makes you angry or scared, check where it came from before you share it.

blank.sentence: A funny picture that people copy, change, and pass along online is a ___.

why: People copy and pass them along, so a post can travel far.
short: Funny picture people copy and share
